scope: Architecture-neutral evidence for Skill Evaluation UI Slice 3
user_job: See which exact shared skill revision is original, published, integrated, experimental, passing, or released.
See what changed between exact revisions without browsing arbitrary plugin files.
Understand progress within a failing task: the earliest failure frontier, failure class, instruction uptake, product movement, blocker, and supporting safe source identifiers.
Find the tasks needing attention across many concurrent local sessions.

existing_authority.completed_correctness: evaluation_history.history() validates immutable evaluator artifacts and is authoritative for completed outcomes.
existing_authority.live_activity: dashboard session and event state is non-final and is superseded by immutable evaluator artifacts.
existing_authority.skill_identity: skill_eval.py skill_identity() records the target skill name, resolved plugin path, and each target-skill file path and SHA-256.
existing_authority.plugin_identity: skill_eval.py directory_identity() records regular-file path, SHA-256, mode, and an aggregate fingerprint while refusing symlinks and non-regular files.
existing_authority.run_snapshot: skill_eval.py snapshot_plugin() copies the complete plugin into each run's target-plugin while excluding Git and cache files and refusing symlinks.
existing_authority.history_projection: evaluation_history.py validates identity artifacts but exposes safe fingerprints rather than full manifests.
existing_authority.dashboard_projection: dashboard_projection.py uses typed readers and does not expose arbitrary files or complete plugin trees.

observed_gaps: No canonical machine-readable artifact declares lineage role or parent/child revision relationships.
No canonical artifact distinguishes published, original, integrated, experimental, passing, and released state.
Existing skill identities contain hashes but not immutable file bytes suitable for durable exact comparison.
Full run snapshots are attempt-local, copy the whole plugin, and are not a safe dashboard browsing surface.
No canonical task-progress artifact records earliest failure frontier, failure classification, instruction uptake, product movement, or blocker.
The current dashboard has campaign and session views but no task-detail route or attention queue.
The current dashboard marks lineage, experiments, cloud work, and ablation unavailable.

lineage: cumulative-skill-hill-climb.md treats independent work as hypotheses for one shared skill or skill-set lineage.
Published revisions become the next baseline only after exact-candidate product, regression, and transfer gates pass.
Experimental revisions must not be presented as released.
task_progress: SKILL.md defines failure classes including skill defect, instruction interaction, execution variance, packet defect, harness defect, and grading defect.
SKILL.md defines instruction uptake statuses OBSERVED, PARTIAL, ABSENT, and NOT_APPLICABLE.
SKILL.md defines product movement as Conquered, Strict improvement, Mixed, No signal, or Regression.
parallel-treatment-search.md requires the earliest remaining failure frontier to be compared against an unchanged control.

supported_callers: The skill-evaluation workflow coordinating a local corpus.
The local evaluator producing immutable attempt artifacts.
Concurrent Copilot sessions registered to the same dashboard campaign.
A loopback browser holding the generation-scoped capability.
security_and_privacy_boundary: The browser must not receive arbitrary filesystem paths, raw plugin directories, hidden judge evidence, candidate workdirs, raw logs, credentials, or unrestricted file content.
Any stored revision bytes must be limited to explicitly named target-skill roots and must refuse symlinks, escapes, and non-regular files.
Raw content-addressed blobs must not have a browser route.
Generated diffs must compare only validated manifests already admitted to the same campaign.
Task-progress records may contain bounded structured summaries and safe identifiers, not arbitrary file attachments or browsing paths.
Malformed, missing, conflicting, or mismatched lineage/progress state must remain unavailable or conflicted rather than falling back to inferred success.
scope_constraints: Loopback-only service and existing generation-scoped capability model.
No remote hosting or broad cloud discovery.
No arbitrary corpus or plugin browsing.
No experiment hypothesis/arm mechanics or distributed-run orchestration in Slice 3.
failure_modes_to_design_for: A lineage declaration references a missing, malformed, or non-admitted snapshot.
Two writers reuse an identifier with different bytes.
A snapshot contains a symlink, escaping path, non-regular file, or changed bytes during capture.
A declared parent is missing, belongs to another campaign, or would create a cycle.
A progress record binds the wrong case revision or snapshot identity.
A progress record claims passing while immutable evaluator results do not.
A diff request attempts to compare unregistered snapshots or read raw blobs.
A current source skill changes after snapshot capture.
Legacy campaigns contain no lineage or progress records.
One corrupt record would otherwise hide valid records from other writers.
observable_acceptance: An installed-plugin dashboard can show an exact original-to-integrated skill comparison generated from immutable admitted snapshots.
A completed PASS appears only when immutable evaluator history matches the exact snapshot identity.
A failing task detail can show a typed failure frontier, failure class, instruction uptake, product movement, and blocker without serving raw evidence files.
Concurrent writers can publish distinct records without overwriting one another.
Malformed, conflicting, cross-campaign, symlinked, or mismatched inputs remain visibly unavailable or conflicted.
Legacy Foundation campaigns continue to render with lineage and task progress explicitly unavailable.
